title: As-of-right taxi licences at a set annual fee (Victoria)
summary: Following the Taxi Industry Inquiry, new taxi licences became available at any time to approved applicants for a set annual fee from 30 June 2014 in metropolitan and urban zones, removing the cap on licence numbers; country zones moved to price notification.

instruments.title: Transport Legislation Amendment (Foundation Taxi and Hire Car Reforms) Act 2013

commenced.what: As-of-right taxi licensing at set annual fees, new zones, and price notification in regional/country zones

direction_rationale: Removing the numerical cap on taxi licences lowers the entry barrier created by scarce perpetual licences (assignment fees), allowing more operators to enter.
comparison: Other states' taxi markets in 2012-15 (before ride-share legalisation)
confounders: Uber entry into Melbourne (unlawful UberX from 2014)
notes: Hire car licence prices also cut in Dec 2013; metro licence values fell 26% in 2013-14 per the TSC report.

assessment.summary: New taxi licences became available at any time to approved applicants for a set annual fee, ending the cap on licence numbers in Melbourne and urban zones.

marks.reason: Ends the numerical cap on taxi licences.

assessment.confidence_note: The archived econometric evaluation found no detectable effect on taxi business entry (grade Weak); ride-share arrived soon after.

responsible.note: The Minister for Public Transport administers the Commercial Passenger Vehicle Industry Act 2017.

history.what: The Commercial Passenger Vehicle Industry Act 2017 came into full operation: taxi licences gave way to registration and accreditation, and ride-share became legal.
